measureRecords.whatItDoes: Establish a town administrator appointed by the Town Council to coordinate daily town administration under the council’s direction and perform other duties the council assigns by ordinance or resolution. The amendment would take effect January 1, 2027, with the first appointment by December 31, 2027. The council would retain appointment, discipline, suspension and removal powers unless the charter provides otherwise.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the administrator position, appointment deadline and retained council powers.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this proposed administrator position and charter change.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Transfer School Department financial and managerial accounting from the town Finance Department to the superintendent and School Committee. School funds would remain with the town treasurer, and payments would remain subject to the finance director’s review, as further provided by ordinance.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the accounting transfer with those custody and payment-review conditions.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this proposed transfer of school accounting responsibility.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Expand the Board of Assessment Review from three members to five qualified town voters appointed by the Town Council. Replace six-year terms with staggered three-year terms.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the five-member board and staggered three-year terms.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this proposed membership and term change.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Increase the annual Capital Reserve Fund contribution from 2% to 4% of the operating budget. Phase it in by 0.25 percentage points each year over eight years, beginning July 1, 2027.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve that eight-year increase from 2% to 4%.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this proposed increase in capital-reserve contributions.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Remove the charter requirement that the emergency management director be a qualified town voter.
measureRecords.noMeans: Keep that qualification in the charter.
